findings.title: forEach(async) fire-and-forget on calendar/video deletions
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` discards the returned promises. The surrounding `try { ... } catch (error) { ... }` cannot catch rejections from inside the async callback, and the caller (reschedule API) returns to the user once the synchronous portion of the loop ends. As a result, calendar `deleteEvent` / `deleteMeeting` calls may still be in flight when the function returns `true` and the reschedule email is sent, leading to inconsistent state (booking marked rescheduled while old events are not yet deleted). This was made worse by the async conversion because both `getCalendar` and the deletion calls are now Promise-returning; before, only `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` were promise-returning. Replace with `for (const bookingRef of bookingRefsFiltered)` and `await` each step, or build an array of promises and `await Promise.all(...)`.

findings.title: forEach(async) fire-and-forget on calendar/video deletions
findings.body: Identical issue to `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts:125`. The async `forEach` callback's promises are dropped, so `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls may not complete (and rejections are uncaught) before this function returns `true` and the reschedule flow continues. Replace with a sequential `for ... of` loop or `Promise.all(...)` over the references.

findings.title: forEach(async) on calendar/video deletions in requestReschedule
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` does not await the returned promises. The function falls straight through to `await sendRequestRescheduleEmail(...)` and the rest of the mutation while the calendar `deleteEvent` and `deleteMeeting` calls are still pending. There is no `try/catch` around the loop either, so any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection. With the new async `getCalendar`, the call now performs a lazy chunk download for every credential in addition to the network call to the provider, making the race more likely to be observed. Convert to `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))` or a sequential `for ... of` with awaited steps.

findings.title: forEach(async) on recurring-event calendar deletions
findings.body: In the recurring-event branch of cancellation, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... })` discards the returned promises, so the function reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` and returns the HTTP response before the per-credential calendar deletions have finished. The outer `try/catch` does not cover this loop either. Because `getCalendar` is now async, this serializes per-credential dynamic chunk loads behind an unawaited loop, widening the race window. Replace with a proper loop that collects promises and lets `Promise.all` drive completion.

findings.title: Resolved value pushed to apiDeletes instead of the promise
findings.body: Inside the unawaited forEach above, `const deletedEvent = await calendar?.deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId); apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent);` pushes the already-resolved value (or `undefined`) into `apiDeletes` rather than the pending Promise. The later `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` therefore never waits for those deleteEvent calls in the recurring-event path (and even if forEach were fixed to await, the push would still capture resolved values). Push the Promise returned by `deleteEvent` directly, i.e. `apiDeletes.push(calendar?.deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId) as Promise<unknown> | undefined);` and let `Promise.all` await it.

findings.title: getVideoAdapters serializes dynamic imports
findings.body: The previous `reduce` implementation ran the entire synchronous mapping in one pass; the new implementation uses a sequential `for (const cred of withCredentials) { const app = await appStore[...]; ... }`, so every credential now blocks the next on its dynamic import + module evaluation. With multiple video credentials attached (Zoom, Daily, Whereby, etc.) this turns into N sequential async chunks where it used to be one synchronous pass and could be N parallel `Promise.all(creds.map(...))` calls. Replace with `Promise.all(withCredentials.map(...))` to keep the parallel cost similar to before.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials is sync but leaks Promise<Calendar> in its result
findings.body: `getCalendarCredentials` was kept synchronous, yet inside it `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` now returns `Promise<Calendar | null>` because `getCalendar` became async. The returned objects therefore carry `calendar: Promise<Calendar | null>`, but the function signature does not advertise that and callers must remember to `await item.calendar` (which is exactly what the new `getConnectedCalendars` body now has to do). Either make `getCalendarCredentials` async and `await getCalendar`, or stop calling `getCalendar` inside it and only return `{ integration, credential }`, leaving adapter construction to the caller. As written, the public type lies about its return value and any future caller that treats `item.calendar` as a sync `Calendar` will get a rejected promise.

findings.title: Awaiting already-resolved apiDeletes entries in seat cancellation
findings.body: After `Promise.all(integrationsToDelete).then(async () => { ... })` resolves, the code schedules `prisma.booking.update` for last-attendee seat cancellation, but `integrationsToDelete` was built by `await getCalendar(credential); integrationsToDelete.push(calendar?.deleteEvent(...))`. Since `deleteEvent` is not awaited here, the pushed value is the unresolved Promise, which is correct. However this pattern is mixed with the broken recurring-event branch (see the other findings on lines 460/466), and the inconsistency makes the file easy to misread. After fixing the recurring branch, ensure the whole file consistently pushes pending Promises into the arrays that `Promise.all` later drains, instead of awaiting-then-pushing.
